summary.headline: Turtlemint Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 40% to INR 294 crores, with adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to minus 9% of revenue from minus 21%.
summary.overview: Platform premium grew 49% YoY to about INR 1,205 crores and revenue grew about 40% to INR 294 crores in Q1 FY27. Service EBITDA rose nearly 90% to INR 39 crores (about 13% of revenue), and corporate overheads fell to 22% of revenue from 30%. Adjusted EBITDA loss was INR 26 crores (minus 9% of revenue) and PAT loss was INR 38 crores (minus 13%), versus a INR 47 crore loss a year earlier. Management reiterated a target of adjusted EBITDA breakeven for the full year, with profitability weighted to H2 given seasonality.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Management implied motor growth of about 50%+ YoY, with PoSP growth and a new Turtlefin platform partner contributing. Motor market Q1 is 16-18% below Q4 and H2 is about 55% of the year.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Q1 health grew about 45%+ YoY. Motor-only DPs starting to sell health grew 40%+ YoY. Nearly half of renewal premium is from health and life.

segments.name: Term life
segments.commentary: Term life grew about 60%+ YoY in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Business expected to grow about 40% YoY for the year, per July post-listing guidance.
Adjusted EBITDA breakeven targeted for full FY27, with profitability weighted to H2; management said PAT should 'not be too far away' but declined to give a PAT timeline.
Service EBITDA margin expected near-term to step up about 2 pp to about 16%, then 18%, reaching about 23-24% over 4-5 years as renewal book grows.
Corporate overheads expected to fall to 7-8% of revenue over 4-5 years (from 22% now).
Fixed costs below service EBITDA expected to rise in line with inflation.
demand_pricing: Digital partner base about 690,000+ after 32,000+ recruits in Q1; Turtlemint Academy ~55,000 monthly active users.
Take rate stable YoY; management said mix shift to renewals is the only change and there was no GST-related impact.
Renewal service EBITDA said to be 2.5-3x new service EBITDA; renewal servicing cost about 0.2% of revenue. Commission cost rises in line with top line.
Insurer relationships: for 17 insurers, Turtlemint's growth contribution was at least 2x industry growth in Q1.
DP attrition: 28-30% in first 24 months, falling to 2-3%; about 65% retained by year 5-6, management said trends unchanged.
Management said PoSP market growing at 30%+ CAGR; claims that Turtlemint has the highest PoSP share among players; competition seen as a 2-3 player market.
Motor TP pricing and commission regulation remain uncertain; management said insurers other than ICICI Lombard are awaiting the GIC appeal before provisioning.

qa_highlights.question: What drives seasonality, given the business is motor-heavy?
qa_highlights.answer: Motor market is about 45% H1 and 55% H2; Q1 is typically 16-18% below Q4. Q1 growth YoY remains strong and Q2, Q3 and Q4 should each be bigger than the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is take rate change driven by renewals or GST, and why did other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Take rate is unchanged; the only shift is renewal vs fresh mix. Service EBITDA improved about 3 pp: roughly 2 pp from non-commission costs and 1 pp from commission costs. Commission rises with volume.

qa_highlights.question: How would commission cuts affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said health saw three full quarters after the GST-related commission reset, with revenue and margin still growing as volume offset the reset. Strategy will be decided once there is more clarity.

qa_highlights.question: How will service EBITDA margin reach 24-25% and how fast will renewal share rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal payout and servicing costs are much lower than new business. Management declined to confirm the 70-80% renewal share, saying renewal premium is growing faster and nearly half of renewal premium is from health and life.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity trend across DP cohorts?
qa_highlights.answer: Older cohorts are also improving. Revenue grew about 40% while P3M Active grew about 30-32%, with the difference attributed to productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI lift long-term EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI is cutting costs and driving growth through personalised onboarding and renewal calling, but it is too early to quantify. AI renewal calls showed a renewal rate 500 bps higher and AI handles 55% of support tickets.

qa_highlights.question: When will PAT break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the adjusted EBITDA breakeven target for FY27 and said PAT is not far off, with ESOP cost about INR 7 crores per quarter. No PAT timeline was given.

risks_watch: Commission regulation and motor TP pricing changes (Supreme Court case; insurers awaiting GIC appeal) could affect payouts and renewal economics.
Seasonality: Q1 is lowest; H2 must carry profitability to meet the FY27 adjusted EBITDA breakeven target.
Mix shift to renewals is the core margin driver; watch renewal share (22% now) and renewal growth versus new.
Competition: management views the market as 2-3 players; new entrants face high tech and distribution barriers.
Track DP activation (P3M Active), cohort productivity and attrition, plus whether AI renewal gains hold.
Corporate overhead ratio trajectory from 22% toward 7-8% over 4-5 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and renewals. Management was more guarded on regulation ('speculative', 'we do not know') and declined to give a PAT timeline or new-vs-renewal margin and renewal-share figures.
key_quotes: Our service EBITDA grew by 89% to INR 39 crores as margins continue to expand.
We also indicated that we'll try really hard for the entire year to be adjusted EBITDA breakeven in the current year.

Renewal from a service EBITDA point of view, if I were to compare renewal service EBITDA to new service EBITDA, renewal service EBITDA is about 2.5 times to 3 times higher than the new service EBITDA.
